transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-05-09
Time: 15:00-15:42 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Ava Kim (Redwood Solutions), Liam O'Connor (Veritas Head of Cloud), Priya Desai (Security Architect), Marco Ruiz (Product), Dana Holt (Compliance)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
- High-level security intake: SOC2/ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS
- Veritas is evaluating deployment modes with strong bias to avoid hosted for regulated telemetry
- Next steps: artifacts exchange and targeted perf & KMS integration session

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samira from Redwood, AE on the account, alongside Jordan, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Liam: Doing well, thanks. We've got Priya and Dana here to cover security and compliance questions, and Marco for product context.
[00:14] Samira: Great. Quick agenda, I want to understand Veritas' security posture and where you'd expect Redwood to fit — hosted, dedicated, or private — and then scope any blockers. Jordan will jump into technical constraints if we need.
[00:30] Priya: To start, SOC2 is table stakes, but we also need ISO 27001 evidence and a clear KMS story — we use Okta for SSO and have a strong requirement for customer-managed keys for certain datasets.
[00:41] Jordan: Understood. We support both hosted with managed KMS and private/dedicated where customer KMS (via AWS KMS or bring-your-own HSM) can be used. There are some differences in audit surface and network controls.
[00:55] Dana: Important for us: audit log retention must be configurable to 7 years for certain entitlements, and logs need to be immutable / tamper-evident for the compliance team. Can Redwood export logs to our ELK or S3 with write-once policy?
[01:13] Jordan: Yes, we can stream audit logs to a customer-owned S3, and for dedicated/private deployments we can also integrate with your SIEM. There are retention policies we can configure; the hosted plan has standard retention windows but we can arrange extended retention under enterprise add-on.
[01:31] Marco: Also curious about data residency — we process customer invoices which have EU PII. If we go hosted, are you able to guarantee EU-only data processing?
[01:44] Samira: We have regional hosting and can pin requests to EU-hosted model instances, but for strict residency and sovereignty we typically recommend Dedicated or Private so you control the infra and keys.
[01:56] Liam: Right — leaning that way. What's the gap between Dedicated and Private? Cost and ops overhead versus control, correct?
[02:05] Jordan: Exactly. Dedicated is Redwood-managed GPU pools reserved for you — predictable throughput, isolation, and we can configure VPC peering. Private is a full control plane in your VPC or on-prem, you manage networking and keys. Private has higher ops lift but gives you the most control over residency and KMS.
[02:22] Priya: For KMS: for some workflows we need CMEK (customer managed encryption keys) with HSM-backed keys and a strict separation of roles. Does Redwood support HSM-backed CMEK on both Dedicated and Private?
[02:34] Jordan: We support HSM-backed CMEK in Private and in Dedicated via customer KMS in the cloud provider (AWS KMS with imported key material or CloudHSM). Hosted has managed keys unless we set up a dedicated key partnership. There are some nuances — we'll share the KB.
[02:48] Dana: How about SSO? We use Okta and SCIM for provisioning. We need RBAC integration and SCIM push for groups and least privilege.
[02:56] Ava: We integrate with SAML SSO and support SCIM for user provisioning on our Console. RBAC roles can be mapped to IdP groups. There is also an audit trail for admin actions.
[03:07] Priya: Is the audit trail tamper-evident or just application-level logs?
[03:11] Jordan: For Dedicated and Private, we can ship immutable logs to your object store and configure integrity checks. Hosted has application-level logs and we maintain write-once append semantics, but for certification we recommend dedicated logging to a customer-owned bucket.
[03:27] Liam: What about data in transit and at rest? Do you use envelope encryption?
[03:31] Jordan: We use TLS1.2+ in transit; at rest it's AES-256. For higher assurance, we offer envelope encryption and integrate with external KMS — so keys never reside in the same network as the instance if you choose private keying.
[03:46] Marco: Are there any known compliance gaps vs ISO 27001? We've got a vendor questionnaire with a few callouts — change management, vulnerability management timelines, and penetration testing cadence.
[03:58] Samira: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and has ISO readouts for infra controls; I'll send the security pack. We also run quarterly pentests and have a vulnerability disclosure program. We'll surface the specifics against your questionnaire.
[04:12] Priya: Excellent. Can you do a live demo of how KMS rotation works? We have a rotation policy of 90 days for certain keys.
[04:19] Jordan: We can demo rotation in Private and Dedicated — in hosted rotation is supported but with managed keys we rotate under the hood. For customer-managed KMS you control rotation schedule. We should probably schedule a hands-on session with our infra folks.
[04:34] Dana: Retention: some logs must be 7 years, others 1 year. Is tiered retention available? Do you support lifecycle policies on the exported buckets?
[04:45] Jordan: Yes — lifecycle policies on customer-owned buckets are the canonical way. We'll configure S3 lifecycle rules or equivalent. For hosted, we have paid add-ons; for Dedicated/Private it's easier because you own the destination.
[04:59] Liam: There was earlier mention of KV cache and inference caching — from a data residency standpoint, where is that cached?
[05:07] Jordan: Cache lives with the serving nodes. For Hosted we shard cache regionally; for Dedicated/Private cache remains within your pool, and for Private you can pin nodes to your VPC so it never leaves. We'll share the architecture diagram.
[05:22] Marco: Any implications for model telemetry? We collect model telemetry for quality improvements but can't send PII to third parties. How do you handle telemetry and opt-outs?
[05:32] Samira: We have telemetry levels; by default we collect anonymized usage metrics. For regulated customers, we can disable telemetry or route telemetry to a customer-owned collector. We'll include that option in the security pack.
[05:45] Priya: On RBAC: can we create scoped service accounts for inference calls, with fine-grained roles (embed-only, generate-only)?
[05:55] Ava: Yes. We support token-level permissions and per-route policies. For Dedicated/Private you can map tokens to specific models and routes, and revoke tokens centrally.
[06:05] Dana: What about retention of generated content? Our policy says generated outputs containing PII must be deleted within 30 days, others 365. Can Redwood enforce per-tenant retention?
[06:17] Jordan: We can configure per-tenant retention for cache and stored logs, and for Hosted we offer retention controls via the Console. For strict deletion guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private so you can enforce lifecycle on storage you own.
[06:31] Liam: Ok, cost is a factor. If we go dedicated or private, what's the typical uplift vs hosted? We need ballpark TCO to evaluate.
[06:40] Samira: We'll send a hosted vs dedicated TCO spreadsheet with examples. Private generally has higher fixed ops costs but can lower unit inference cost at scale depending on utilization. We'll include assumptions for GPU types and utilization.
[06:56] Marco: On the topic of model rollouts and fallback — if a model variant is unavailable, do you have automatic fallback to a compatible variant to preserve SLA?
[07:06] Jordan: Yes, smart routing can fallback to pinned variants per policy. For Dedicated, we can pre-provision compatible variants. We'll walk through rollback and canary strategies in the perf walkthrough.
[07:18] Priya: Any certifications for their cloud providers? If we do Dedicated in AWS eu-west-1, do you rely on AWS controls?
[07:25] Samira: We rely on the underlying cloud provider for physical controls; our compliance pack maps our controls to cloud provider attestations. We'll provide the mapping for your compliance team.
[07:37] Dana: For legal evidence we need audit trails that show admin actions and access to keys. Can you provide logs for key access and admin changes?
[07:47] Jordan: Key access logs are available via cloud KMS audit logs when integrated; admin actions in the Redwood Console generate events that can be exported. For Private deployments we can ship all control-plane events to your SIEM.
[07:59] Liam: Ok, timeline — we'd like to decide in the next 4–6 weeks for a pilot. Is that feasible?
[08:07] Samira: Yes, typical pilot timeline is 2–4 weeks for a minimal pilot if we focus scope. If you need Private on-prem, that pushes the timeline due to infra setup. For Dedicated in your cloud region, we can spin up reserved pools faster.
[08:20] Marco: What would you need from us to start a pilot?
[08:23] Jordan: A small sample dataset (sanitized), expected QPS, model choice, and the target residency region. Also, a list of integration points — IdP SAML metadata, KMS key ARN if CMEK, and logging destination.
[08:36] Priya: We can't share raw PII for testing. Would you accept synthetic or masked data?
[08:40] Jordan: Absolutely, synthetic or masked data is fine and preferred for an initial bench. We also support running tests with redacted payloads.
[08:49] Dana: Are there controls for who can start a rollout? We need approvals for production canaries.
[08:54] Ava: We support RBAC gates — only specific admin roles can trigger rollouts. Integrations with ticketing or approval workflows is something we can discuss with your SRE.
[09:06] Liam: Let's talk about incident response — if there's a security incident affecting inference, what's your RTO/RPO commitments under Dedicated/Private?
[09:15] Samira: SLA/RTO commitments are part of enterprise contracts. Dedicated comes with latency and uptime SLAs and on-call support. Private has different responsibilities — since it's customer-managed infra, we provide playbooks and can integrate with your on-call. We'll send an incident response runbook.
[09:32] Priya: For ISO evidence, do you provide artifact packages or just statements?
[09:36] Samira: We provide an ISO scope summary and can share redacted evidence where allowed. We'll include a package that maps controls to evidence for your auditors.
[09:46] Marco: Competitors question — we've looked at CloudServe and AtlasAI. Any direct differences you want to call out on security?
[09:54] Jordan: A quick note: Redwood's differentiation is unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and clearer controls around KMS integration and audit exports. We'll provide a one-pager comparing the options and pointing to the control mappings.
[10:09] Liam: Sounds good. A couple of nitty-gritty questions — do you have SOC2 for the management plane and for telemetry processing?
[10:18] Samira: Yes, SOC2 covers our control plane and data processing for hosted services; we'll share the SOC2 report summary and a statement on telemetry scoping.
[10:27] Priya: Are you able to do a security workshop with our auditors? They like a live Q&A after they review artifacts.
[10:33] Samira: We do auditor Q&A sessions with NDAs. We can schedule that once you sign the NDA and we exchange docs.
[10:41] Liam: On retention again — will you enforce deletion if we ask to purge tenant data? We need attestations that data can be fully removed on termination.
[10:51] Jordan: We have tenant delete flows; for Dedicated/Private you control storage which simplifies it. For hosted we provide deletion certificates and can purge keys and data per contract. We'll include deletion cert language in the sample contract.
[11:05] Marco: Anything to flag about network egress — is there any data that leaves region for model orchestration?
[11:12] Jordan: For hosted we may orchestrate some control-plane operations from our control plane; for Dedicated/Private control plane can be localized or customer-managed. We'll document data paths and can show network diagrams.
[11:25] Priya: Ok, two more things: do you support customer-managed audit retention policies at route level and are logs PII-redacted automatically?
[11:34] Ava: Retention per route is possible on Dedicated/Private. Logs are not automatically PII-redacted — that's usually done upstream by customers or with our optional redaction tooling; we can discuss redaction patterns in the tech session.
[11:49] Dana: If we use a BYOK model with HSM, do you have split-key or K-of-N key management support?
[11:57] Jordan: We support imported key material and CloudHSM. For split-key schemes we can integrate with your HSM provider, but note integration complexity; we'll detail approaches.
[12:09] Samira: We're ~12 minutes in; wanted to make sure we capture the next steps. I'll summarize soon but Jordan anything else to add about perf or benchmarks?
[12:19] Jordan: For the perf walkthrough we'll need a sample workload and desired latency targets. We'll demonstrate batching, KV cache behavior and show how quantization impacts throughput and cost.
[12:30] Marco: On quantization — do you support 4-bit or int8 variants out of the box?
[12:34] Jordan: We support quantized variants where compatible; we'll surface what's verified in our model catalog and recommended tradeoffs for quality vs cost.
[12:44] Priya: For legal sign-off, we need to validate data flow diagrams. Can you produce a data flow diagram showing where keys, caches, and logs move for both dedicated and private options?
[12:53] Samira: Yes, we'll produce data flow diagrams for the three deployment modes.
[12:59] Liam: Ok — can you also include an estimate of time to onboard if we pick Dedicated in eu-west-1?
[13:06] Samira: Typical onboarding for Dedicated is 2–4 weeks including network setup and key exchange. We'll include a more detailed timeline in the follow-up.
[13:18] Dana: One wrinkle — our compliance team will require a 3rd-party security assessment for any vendor that touches PII. Are you open to supporting that?
[13:26] Samira: Yes, we've supported assessments and can coordinate. We'll need to align on scope and NDAs.
[13:33] Liam: Great. Any final questions from Veritas team?
[13:37] Marco: Not yet — we'll review artifacts once you send them.
[13:40] Priya: Please include specifics on key rotation and key access auditing in the pack.
[13:44] Samira: Noted.
[13:47] Jordan: I'll own key rotation docs and the benchmark runbook.
[13:51] Samira: Cool. Quick recap of next steps: Samira to send SOC2/ISO pack and KMS whitepaper; Samira to send TCO spreadsheet; Jordan to prep perf runbook; Veritas to share data residency and retention policy and sample (masked) dataset. We'll set the perf walkthrough for the week of 2028-05-15.
[14:14] Liam: That works. Thanks everyone.
[14:18] Dana: Thanks, speak soon.
[14:21] Marco: Thanks.
[14:23] Samira: Thanks all — I'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
